explanations.explanation: Mountains it is, friend. Jesus says, “…then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.” That's the whole direction, short and clear. I wish my recipes were that easy to follow.

I see why that one tempts you, but the temple isn't in this verse at all. Jesus says, “…then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.” Put your pick next to the verse and the mountains win. Easy mix-up when you're rushing, and I've rushed a batch or two myself.

Close, but the city never comes up in this verse. Jesus says, “…then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.” The direction He gives is the mountains. Keep that one in your back pocket, baker.

I can see why you'd say that. Grabbing a cloak sounds reasonable. But Jesus says, “And let no one in the field return for his cloak.” So the answer is False. The person in the field doesn't go back for it.

That's right. Jesus says, “And let no one in the field return for his cloak.” The person working out in the field doesn't go back for it. I'd be standing there staring at my own apron, but that's the instruction.
Yes, friend. Jesus says, “How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!” I think this line hurts a little. Jesus names them, and it's good to slow down and notice who He names.
No kings in this verse, baker. Jesus says, “How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!” He names the mothers. I think it's a tender line, so it's worth getting it right.

That's not who Jesus names here. He says, “How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!” Priests and scribes don't show up in this verse. The mothers do, and I think that line carries some weight.

Winter, you got it. Jesus says, “Pray that your flight will not occur in the winter or on the Sabbath.” He gives two things to pray about, and the season is the first one. Keep both in your head, baker.
Not spring, friend. Jesus says, “Pray that your flight will not occur in the winter or on the Sabbath.” The season He names is winter. Spring sounds nicer, I'll give you that.

Autumn gets my vote for coziest oven weather, baker, but it isn't on Jesus' list. He says, “Pray that your flight will not occur in the winter or on the Sabbath.” Winter is the season He names, so that's the one to remember.

True. Jesus says there will be “…great tribulation, unseen from the beginning of the world until now, and never to be seen again.” Nothing like it has come before, and nothing like it will come after. That's a heavy line, so let it settle a second.

It's actually True, friend. Jesus says there will be “…great tribulation, unseen from the beginning of the world until now, and never to be seen again.” So there's been nothing like it since the beginning of the world. It's a heavy one, so take your time with it.

Cut short, yes. Jesus says, “But for the sake of the elect, those days will be cut short.” And look at the line before it: if the days had not been cut short, nobody would be saved. That's the sentence to hang onto, baker.
Not put off, friend. Jesus says, “But for the sake of the elect, those days will be cut short.” He's talking about shortening them, not delaying them. Hold onto that.
That's the opposite of what Jesus says. He says, “But for the sake of the elect, those days will be cut short.” Shortened, baker, not stretched.

That's it. Jesus says, “At that time, if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ do not believe it.” No chasing and no second-guessing. Sometimes the plainest instruction is the best one.

I get the urge to check it out, but that's not what Jesus says. He says, “do not believe it.” In verse 26 He adds that if they say He's in the wilderness, “do not go out…” So the answer is not to go looking.
Asking someone sounds sensible, but the priests don't come up here. Jesus says, “do not believe it.” That's the whole instruction in this verse.

It's actually False, friend. Jesus says false Christs and false prophets “…will appear and perform great signs and wonders to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” So they WILL perform signs and wonders. And Jesus adds, “See, I have told you in advance.”

False is right. Jesus says false Christs and false prophets “…will appear and perform great signs and wonders to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” So they do perform signs and wonders. A good show doesn't make it the real thing.

Yes, the elect. Jesus says they will perform great signs and wonders “…to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” That little phrase, if that were possible, is worth noticing. It tells you how strong the deception will be.

Not the Pharisees, friend. Jesus says the signs and wonders are “…to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” The elect are the ones He names here. Good thing it's right there in the text, baker.

The scribes aren't named in this verse, friend. Jesus says the signs and wonders are “…to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” So the elect are the answer. Check the verse and it points right to them.

Lightning, you got it. Jesus says, “For just as the lightning comes from the east and flashes as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.” East to west, all in one flash. That's a picture you won't forget.

Wind is a fair guess, but Jesus doesn't say wind. He says, “For just as the lightning comes from the east and flashes as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.” It's lightning, baker.

Fire is dramatic, I know, and I live next to an oven. But Jesus says, “For just as the lightning comes from the east and flashes as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.” The answer is lightning.
Yes, friend. Jesus says, “the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.” The sun and moon go dark, and the stars fall. I'd be grabbing my hat for that.

Not quite, baker. Jesus says, “the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.” That's what He says the stars do. Hold onto that line, friend, and the sky will make sense.
Not standing still, baker. Jesus says, “the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.” The stars fall, and the powers of the heavens are shaken.

On the clouds of heaven, yes. Jesus says, “They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” That's the picture He gives, and it's a big one. I love that you got it.

Mountains do show up earlier in this talk, friend, but not here. Jesus says, “They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” He comes on the clouds of heaven, baker.

Temple gates, baker? I looked for a gate in that verse and came up empty-handed. Jesus says, “They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” The clouds are the answer.
Angels, right. Jesus says, “And He will send out His angels with a loud trumpet call…” They go out together with the trumpet. I think that's quite a sound.

Prophets is a fair guess, friend, since Jesus talks about the prophet Daniel earlier in this passage (Matthew 24:15). But here the Son of Man sends out someone else. Jesus says, “And He will send out His angels with a loud trumpet call, and they will gather His elect from the four winds…” So the answer is angels, and they're the ones doing the gathering.
Disciples is a fair guess, friend, but they aren't who He sends. Jesus says, “And He will send out His angels with a loud trumpet call…” So the answer is angels.
True, friend. Jesus says they “…will gather His elect from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.” That's from every direction. Nobody gets missed.
It's actually True. Jesus says they “…will gather His elect from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.” That's a wide gathering. I think that's a comforting line.
Yes, baker. Jesus says, “As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.” Tender branches and new leaves are the signal. A fig tree never needs a timer.

explanations.answer: Lose every leaf and go bare
explanations.explanation: That's backward from what Jesus says. He says, “As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.” Leaves sprouting, baker, not falling off.
Bending down isn't in the verse. Jesus says, “As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.” Tender branches and new leaves are the sign.

explanations.answer: He is right at the door
explanations.explanation: Right at the door, yes. Jesus says, “So also, when you see all these things, you will know that He is near, right at the door.” Just like the leaves tell you summer is near. Near, baker, not far.

explanations.answer: He is out in the wilderness
explanations.explanation: That's the line Jesus warned them about earlier. He said that if people say He's in the wilderness, “do not go out…” This time He says, “…you will know that He is near, right at the door.” The answer is right at the door.

explanations.answer: He is still a long way off
explanations.explanation: Not a long way off, friend. Jesus says, “…you will know that He is near, right at the door.” Near is the word He uses. That's the one to remember.
True. Jesus says, “Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.” Heaven and earth pass away, but His words don't. I'd stake my whole bakery on that, baker.
It's actually True. Jesus says, “Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.” Heaven and earth pass, but His words do not. Even my ovens aren't that steady.
